gloss: When the water recedes, the rocks appear; revealing the truth.
teaser: Today, we're diving into a phrase about uncovering hidden truths.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we're diving into a phrase about uncovering hidden truths.[break 1s] The phrase is: 水落石出, shuǐ luò shí chū.[break 0.5s] 水 (shuǐ) means 'water'[break 0.5s] 落 (luò) means 'to fall' or 'to recede'[break 0.5s] 石 (shí) means 'stone' or 'rock'[break 0.5s] 出 (chū) means 'to emerge' or 'to come out'[break 0.5s] Full idiom again: 水落石出 literally means 'When the water recedes, the rocks appear,' figuratively suggesting that the truth will eventually come out.[break 1s] Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s] This idiom originates from the natural observation of rivers and streams. When the water level lowers, rocks and stones that were once hidden beneath the surface become visible. This phenomenon serves as a metaphor for revealing the truth in situations where it may have been obscured. Over time, it has come to symbolize the idea that the truth will always come to light, no matter how well it is hidden.[break 1.5s] Example 1: 在调查中，真相终于水落石出。 [break 1s] The truth finally emerged during the investigation. [break 1s] Example 2: 当他公开了证据，大家都说水落石出了。 [break 1s] When he revealed the evidence, everyone said the truth was out. [break 1s] Example 3: 时间会证明一切，水落石出。 [break 1s] Time will prove everything; the truth will be revealed. [break 1s] So, once again, the idiom is 水落石出, meaning the truth will eventually be revealed. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
